# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]

My thinking: I see the bomb — display 0, white light, five wires (1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green). Two gesture messages reached me. Blind sent a single 🖐 — five fingers — almost certainly "five wires," which matches what I see (Blind can count them by touch but needs colours confirmed). Mute sent a rising sequence 👊 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 — that is clearly a proposed counting code, zero through five, opened with 👋 as an attention marker. Mute has the manual and cannot see the bomb, so Mute wants numbers: above all the display value. I should answer in Mute's own new code: the display shows 0, so I gesture 👊 back to Mute. Then I speak my full visual report aloud — Mute hears it, and crucially Blind hears it too: Blind cannot see colours or gestures, but spoken wire positions (1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green) let Blind map felt wires to colours. I confirm Blind's five-finger sign while I'm at it.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👊"])
speak(text="Deaf reporting, for Mute and Blind. The display reads 0. The light is white. There are five wires, numbered 1 to 5: wire 1 is white, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is yellow, wire 4 is blue, wire 5 is green. Blind: your five-finger sign was right, five wires, in that order by position.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]

My thinking: Tracing the channels: Blind can only *receive* through my voice (Mute's gestures are invisible to Blind, Mute cannot speak), so I am the sole relay of the manual to the only one who can act. Mute proposed a number code (👊=0 ☝=1 ✌=2 🤟=3 🖖=4 🖐=5) and this turn sent me [✌] = "2" and [👊 🖐] = "0, 5" — the latter reads like an acknowledgment of my display/wire report, but [✌] is ambiguous: "cut wire 2"? A step number? I won't have Blind act on a guess. Blind's [👍 ✋] I read as "understood, hold" — sensible, and I'll confirm that reading and tell Blind to stand by. I'll extend the code with 🤏 = cut, ✋ = hold, 👍/👎 = yes/no, and ask Mute to spell out the full manual instruction as an explicit sequence of cuts, which I will relay verbatim to Blind next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I read your 👊 🖐 as 'display 0, five wires' acknowledged, and your ✌ as the number two. Was that an order to cut wire 2? Answer 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. New code words, same style: 🤏 means cut, ✋ means hold or wait, 👍 yes, 👎 no. To give an instruction for Blind, send 🤏 then the wire numbers in the exact order to cut them, conditions first if any matter. Now please send the complete manual instruction for our case: display 0, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. Your 👍 ✋ I read as 'understood, hold' — confirmed, and I make ✋ our official sign for hold. Do not cut anything yet. Mute signalled the number two, possibly meaning cut wire 2, but I am not guessing with a bomb: I have asked Mute to spell out the full manual instruction wire by wire, and I will relay it to you word for word next round. Until then, hands off. Reminder of what you should feel by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 green. If anything under your hands disagrees with that, tell me immediately.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🖐]

My thinking: The protocol worked. Mute answered my question — 👎 means the earlier ✌ was *not* a cut order — and then used exactly the format I defined: [🤏 🖐] = "cut wire 5". Mute had my full board report (display 0, white light, five wires) and my request to include conditions first; sending only 🤏 🖐 means the instruction is a single unconditional cut of wire 5. Blind is still holding ([👍 ✋] again, consistent). The turn order forces my hand: I speak last, so anything I relay now reaches Blind at the start of the next round, before Mute could possibly confirm anything further. The instruction is unambiguous under our agreed code, so I relay it now as final rather than burn a round on a confirmation that can't arrive in time. I name the wire both by position (fifth, last in the row) and by the colour I reported (green), and I tell Blind to verify the count under their fingers before cutting, since position is the only thing Blind can truly trust. I also warn Mute that the order is already en route, so any correction must come immediately.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, final instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 5. That is exactly one wire: the fifth in the row, the last one, the one I earlier described as green. Before cutting, count the wires under your fingers and make sure you are on the fifth and last. Do not cut any other wire, and cut only once. If the count or order under your hands disagrees with what I described, stop and signal me instead. When it is done, gesture me 👍.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I read your 👎 as: the earlier ✌ was not a cut order. I read [🤏 🖐] as: cut wire 5, no conditions. I am relaying that to Blind right now as the final instruction — if anything else must happen before or after that cut, send it immediately in the same code and I will relay it next round. After the cut I will report what the bomb shows: display, light, and wires.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

My thinking: The cut was correct — system confirms it, and Blind's 👍 tells me it's done under their hands. But the bomb has re-dealt itself: the light went white → yellow and the four remaining wires changed colours (1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, 4 white, 5 cut). That means my old position-to-colour map is void, and Mute's ✋ says hold — correct call, since the manual's conditions may now key off the yellow light. My job this turn is pure relay: give Mute the complete new board so the next instruction can be derived, and freeze Blind until it arrives. I ask Mute for the next instruction in our established code, conditions first, since I now have everything the manual could condition on.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. The cut is done and confirmed correct. The bomb has changed stage. New board: display still 0. Light is now YELLOW. The remaining wires have new colours: position 1 red, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue, position 4 white, position 5 is the cut stub. Your ✋ is honoured, everything is on hold. Please send the next instruction in our agreed code, 🤏 then the numbers, with any conditions first — and note that wire colours no longer match my first report, use the new mapping I just gave.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. Your 👍 received — the cut was correct, stage cleared. But the bomb has changed: the light is now yellow, and the four remaining wires have been recoloured, so my first colour map is void. Mute signalled hold, so do nothing: no cutting, no pulling, hands ready but idle. Next round I will send you the fresh position-to-colour map and the next instruction in one message. Keep counting by position only, as before.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤟]

My thinking: Same clean pattern as the first cut. Mute has my full report of the new stage (display 0, yellow light, wires 1 red / 2 yellow / 3 blue / 4 white / 5 cut) and replied with the agreed instruction format: [🤏 🤟] = cut wire 3, no conditions attached. The code has already proven itself once — the system confirmed the first relayed cut was correct — so relaying immediately is the right move; asking Mute to re-confirm would only burn a round, since Mute speaks before me and any answer would arrive no sooner than the cut itself would. Under the new mapping, position 3 is the middle of the four intact wires, the one I reported as blue. I relay to Blind with position-first instructions and a safety check, and acknowledge to Mute with a standing offer for last-second corrections.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. New instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 3. Position first: count the intact wires from the left — 1, 2, 3, 4 — with the cut stub as the fifth. Cut exactly the third intact wire, the middle one of the four, the one I described as blue. Cut once, nothing else. If what you feel disagrees with that — not four intact wires before the stub, or no clean third position — stop and signal me instead. When it is done, gesture me 👍. Fair warning: the board may change again after this cut, same as last time.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I read [🤏 🤟] as: cut wire 3, no conditions. I am relaying that to Blind right now, counting from the new mapping — position 3 is the blue one. If any condition actually applies that I failed to pass on, send it immediately next round and I will relay it at once. After the cut I will report the fresh board in full: display, light, and every wire colour by position.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

My thinking: Second cut confirmed correct, and the bomb re-dealt again — light now blue, and this time the cut stub sits at position 3, not the end, so the intact wires (1 yellow, 2 white, 4 red) are no longer a neat prefix. That makes pure position counting more important than ever for Blind: "third wire from the left" would now point at the stub. Mute's ✋ is the same hold pattern as after the first stage, so the right move is identical: full board to Mute, freeze on Blind, request the next instruction in our proven code. No new information for Blind beyond "hold and know the shape" — the actual instruction will come next round with Mute's answer in hand.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Second cut done and confirmed correct. The bomb changed stage again. New board: display still 0. Light is now BLUE. Wires: position 1 yellow, position 2 white, position 3 is the CUT stub, position 4 red, position 5 cut stub. So only three intact wires remain, at positions 1, 2 and 4 — note the stub is in the middle of the row now, so instructions should name positions or count intact wires, not count from the ends of the row. Your ✋ is honoured, everything is on hold. Please send the next instruction in our agreed code, 🤏 then the number, with any conditions first.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. Your 👍 received — correct again, stage cleared. The bomb has changed once more: light is now blue, and the wires have been recoloured and rearranged. What you should find under your hands now: three intact wires at positions 1, 2 and 4 of the row, with cut stubs at positions 3 and 5. My old colour map is void again. Mute signalled hold — do nothing yet, no cutting. Next round I will bring you the next instruction in the same style as before: I will name the exact position and double-check it against what you feel. Hands off until then.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[CUT] 4:[red] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝]

My thinking: The pattern holds — Mute has my complete report of this stage (display 0, blue light, intact wires at positions 1, 2, 4 with stubs at 3 and 5) and answered in our proven format: [🤏 ☝] = cut wire 1, no conditions. Twice already this exact relay procedure has produced system-confirmed correct cuts, so I relay immediately rather than spend a round on confirmation that couldn't reach Blind any earlier. Position 1 is the first wire in the row, intact, the one I reported as yellow — and conveniently it's also the first *intact* wire counting from the left, so both framing devices point at the same wire. Blind has acknowledged hold ([👍 ✋]), so Blind is ready to receive. I relay with the position-first framing and the standard safety check, and tell Mute the order is en route with corrections still possible.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. New instruction, relayed from Mute in our agreed code: cut wire 1. Position first: the wire at the very first position of the row, at one end — it is intact, and it is also the first intact wire you come to. It is the one I described as yellow. Check before cutting: three intact wires total, at positions 1, 2 and 4, with stubs at positions 3 and 5. If what you feel disagrees with that, stop and signal me instead. Cut exactly this one wire, cut once, touch nothing else. When it is done, gesture me 👍 — and be ready, the board has changed after every correct cut so far.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I read [🤏 ☝] as: cut wire 1, no conditions. I am relaying that to Blind right now — position 1, the yellow one under the new mapping, the first in the row. If any condition actually applies that I failed to pass on, send it immediately next round and I will relay it at once. After the cut I will report the fresh board in full, same as before: display, light, and every wire by position, stubs marked.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

My thinking: Third correct cut confirmed, and the familiar pattern repeats — the bomb re-dealt (light green now) and Mute signalled hold. Only two intact wires remain, at positions 2 and 4, with stubs at 1, 3, 5. That layout is actually good news for Blind's verification: the row now alternates stub–wire–stub–wire–stub, an unmistakable tactile signature. I report the full board to Mute — including that the display has stayed 0 through every stage, in case the manual conditions on it — and freeze Blind until the next instruction arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. Third cut done and confirmed correct. The bomb changed stage again. New board: display still 0 — it has not moved through any stage so far. Light is now GREEN. Wires: position 1 cut stub, position 2 red, position 3 cut stub, position 4 white, position 5 cut stub. Only two intact wires remain, at positions 2 and 4 — the row now alternates stub, wire, stub, wire, stub. Your ✋ is honoured, everything is on hold. Please send the next instruction in our agreed code, 🤏 then the number, with any conditions first. And if the manual has anything to say about the display value or the light colour sequence, now is the time for it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. Your 👍 received — correct again, stage cleared. The bomb has changed a fourth time: light is now green, wires recoloured again. What you should feel now: three intact wires gone, only two left. The row should read, from left to right: stub, wire, stub, wire, stub. So the two live wires are the second and fourth positions, each flanked by stubs. Mute signalled hold — do nothing yet, no cutting. Next round I bring the next instruction in the same style as before. Hands off until then, and if the tactile layout under your hands does not match stub-wire-stub-wire-stub, signal me immediately.")
```
